responsibility: `rustc_query_system` provides the compiler’s generic query and incremental-reuse infrastructure, supplying the machinery that lets rustc compute demand-driven results, track the dependencies those computations used, and safely reuse prior work across and within compilations. Its crate root (`lib.rs`) assembles this subsystem by wiring together the query runtime, dependency graph, and incremental hashing support, re-exporting the core query-system value and error types, and registering the crate’s diagnostics. The `query` module forms the main execution engine: it defines the shared query context and per-query configuration, the cache interfaces and concrete query-result storage, the active-job/waiting/cycle management for parallel execution, and the logic for lookup, execution, dependency recording, forcing, disk loading, and recovery. The `dep_graph` module supplies the incremental dependency-tracking side of that engine by defining dep-node identities and work-product IDs, the interfaces that connect query execution to dependency recording and cache loading, the in-memory and serialized dependency graph representations, red/green tracking, and inspection/debug support for graph structure. The `ich` module provides the stable hashing layer that makes incremental reuse sound, defining the hashing context and policies for deterministically hashing compiler data, syntax, spans, and HIR bodies using stable identities and session-derived source information. Supporting these core modules, `cache.rs` defines a small non-query cache that couples cached lookup results with the dep-graph node that produced them so later reads mark the right dependency as used, `values.rs` defines the trait and default behavior for producing query values in the presence of dependency cycles, and `error.rs` defines the structured diagnostics for query-system failures and recovery conditions such as cycles, reentrancy, dep-graph inconsistencies, and recursion overflow. Together, these pieces make `rustc_query_system` the reusable foundation for rustc’s query-based execution model and incremental compilation bookkeeping.
